correctness.rationale: All integers with Omega at most two are 1, a prime, a prime square, or a product of two distinct primes. The proof treats every ordered combination compatible with consecutiveness. Prime-square/semiprime cases contradict AM-GM, and the squarefree-semiprime parity split yields either (q-2)(s-2)=3 or the impossible equation (p-2)(r-2)=-3. Only (4,5) and (14,15) survive, and both are directly verified. A fresh exact checker corroborates the classification below 100000.

value.rationale: Consecutive Dedekind-psi collisions are explicitly tracked by A291043, so the collision equation is a natural studied object. The Omega<=2 restriction is the complete first multiplicative-complexity boundary for a multiplicative function, not a numerical cutoff. The result explains exactly why the first two low-complexity collisions split into one squarefree sigma-inherited pair and one genuinely Dedekind-psi prime-square pair.
